subject: DPA — retention safety-net / backup & DR carve-out (proposed language)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@citadelai.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@citadelai.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA: retention carve-out for backup/DR copies — initial ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Citadel AI is comfortable with the bulk of Redwood's DPA, but our security/legal team flagged the need for explicit carve-out language allowing short-term retention of encrypted backup and DR copies that may persist beyond primary deletion windows for operational recovery.

Key asks:
- A short "safety-net" exception that permits immutable backups to be retained for up to 90 days after a deletion request strictly for recovery and disaster-recovery validation.
- Clear restrictions that backups are encrypted, access-controlled, and not used for processing or analytics.
- Agreement that restoration of backup copies for customer data requires documented request and will be recorded in audit logs.

I'm attaching a very short redline proposal to show the exact wording we have in mind. Can you loop in legal/infra to confirm Redwood's operational constraints? We'd like to resolve this before the DocuSign execution.

Attachment: proposed-DPA-safety-net-redline.docx (DOCX)

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Security Contracts, Citadel AI
[sent from mobile]

Subject: Fw: DPA: retention carve-out for backup/DR copies — initial ask

Neha / Karthik — forwarding Samira's note and the proposed language. At a high level Citadel wants a 90-day safety-net for encrypted backups, explicit prohibition on using backups for analytics, and logging for any restore. They want to finalize this before we send the DPA for signature. Can legal confirm whether this language is acceptable and infra confirm operationally we can commit to the 90-day window and audit requirements?

Samira — looping in our legal and infra leads. Thanks for the clear ask.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@citadelai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: retention carve-out for backup/DR copies — proposed redlines

Thanks Marissa / Samira — reviewed the proposed wording. We can accept a narrowly-scoped backup/DR carve-out provided we add safeguards so the exception cannot be repurposed (e.g., for data processing). Proposed changes (high-level):
- Limit exception to "encrypted, immutable backup and disaster-recovery copies retained only for restoration purposes."
- Retention cap: 60 days after a deletion request (instead of 90) to balance operational recovery needs and our data minimization policy.
- Prohibit processing or analytics on backup copies; any restoration requires an internal ticket with requestor, justification, and will be recorded in audit logs.
- Require customer to provide documented request for restoration; Redwood will notify the customer of restoration events and retention of restored data.

I've attached inline redlines to the DPA (see attachment). Karthik / Vivek — can your teams live with 60 days and the audit/notification requirements? If not, please propose operationally acceptable alternatives.

Attachment: proposed-DPA-safety-net-redline.docx (with legal comments)

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@citadelai.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@citadelai.com>, legal@citadelai.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: retention carve-out for backup/DR copies — proposed redlines

Neha — thanks for the quick review. Citadel legal is sympathetic to operational constraints, but 60 days is tight for some of our longer RTO/RPO testing windows. Can we meet in the middle at 75 days? Also, we appreciate the processing prohibition but want explicit language that backups will only be used for restoration and for disaster recovery testing on a de-identified basis (if needed).

We can accept strict audit logging and documented restoration requests. If Redwood can add the de-identification-only-for-testing exception (with strict controls), we should be able to sign.

— Tom
Tom Reeves
Senior Counsel, Citadel AI
[Attachment: none]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@citadelai.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: retention carve-out for backup/DR copies — infra input

Short answer: we can operationally support a 75-day window, but with caveats. Notes from infra:
- Backups are encrypted at rest and we control KMS keys; retention is configurable by policy, but some legacy snapshot chains may cause retention beyond target unless we run a GC job — we can commit to running GC weekly to meet the 75-day SLA.
- De-identification for DR testing: we can provide a process to sanitize data extracts for testing, but it will add 2–3 business days to any scheduled drill.
- Auditability: we can add restore-ticket linking and an immutable log entry for each restore event (ticket id, approver, timestamp).

If legal is okay with the 75-day retention and the added note that testing de-identification may have a short operational lead time, we can accept the language.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@citadelai.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@citadelai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: Final DPA redline — proposed compromise + DocuSign link

Tom / Samira — thanks. Based on infra's confirmation, Redwood can accept the following compromise:
- Backup/DR exception limited to "encrypted, immutable backup and disaster-recovery copies retained solely for restoration and DR testing;"
- Retention cap of 75 days after a deletion request;
- Explicit prohibition on processing backups for analytics; de-identified extracts for DR testing permitted subject to documented controls and a 48–72 hour operational lead time;
- All restores tied to an internal ticket and recorded in immutable audit logs; customer notified within 24 hours of any restore.

I've applied these changes to the DPA and uploaded the DocuSign envelope. Please sign the attached DPA at: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABC123456789

Attachment: proposed-DPA-safety-net-redline.docx (final)

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
